evidence_required: Exact competence-specific request/result/orchestration schema and outbound snapshot results.
Authorized PostgreSQL Task/Outcome/evidence record selection and typed quotation isolation evidence.
Pending MessageEnvelope, matching classification, ordinary-task idempotency, and kind-mismatch no-effect evidence.
Pre/post-I/O, classification-write, task-write, revoke, and archive race evidence.
No fallback/fake/canned production output, no auth/UI/Bus/Timeline replay egress, and safe audit/redaction evidence.
Deterministic timeout, provider error, invalid output, exact fake/spy call count, and unbound-production evidence.
purpose: Make the canonical task_follow_up roster member operational as a provider-neutral, permission-aware competence whose only possible product effect is one matched ordinary Task through existing project classification and PostgreSQL authority.
success_outcome: One strict provider-neutral task_follow_up invocation over current authorized PostgreSQL Task/Outcome/evidence records can emit only a check, measurement, or follow_up proposal; after model I/O it commits exactly one immutable run/fingerprint runtime disposition as publication_denied or envelope_handed_off with one post-guard message. A matching classification and current ordinary-task guard then create exactly one same-kind Task through the existing classified disposition and sole Task writer. Same-run retry/conflict/concurrency, restore, audit/commit failure, and runtime-versus-classified races create no replay or contradictory effect; new evaluation requires new command/run/message identities. W1 Outcome evidence remains closed while the competence uses a separate source resolver. Deterministic acceptance remains provider-neutral with no provider/model/base URL/credential/egress/network/live-smoke requirement or claim.
anti_goals: Do not widen generic ProviderRequestV1, MessageEnvelope, Safety classification, or roster identity contracts.
Do not let the model approve/reject, create action, complete Tasks, record Outcomes, mutate Plant state, invoke tools/devices, or bypass TASK-039 authority.
Do not add a public agent endpoint, UI/Bus/Timeline replay context, agent memory, tools, RAG, fallback model, fake production output, or silent failure substitution.
Do not add a generic Agent Runtime ledger, persist/replay MessageEnvelope or candidate/provider payloads, or weaken the existing classified disposition schema to represent pre-classification denial.
Do not claim FT-012 acceptance from transport-only, schema-only, fake-production, fallback, or blocked/failed output; require the complete deterministic authority and fake/spy evidence matrix.

forbidden_scope: TASK-039 database schema, HTTP contract, or lifecycle semantics except a narrowly proven compatibility repair.
Generic ProviderRequestV1, MessageEnvelope, SafetyClassificationResultV1, or canonical roster identity widening.
Frontend/PWA, public agent API, Agent Chat Bus task payload, UI Feed context, Timeline replay, raw chat, or governance fields outside the registered Task Follow-Up request allowlist.
Approval/action/completion/Outcome/Plant-state/device authority, automated actuation, tools, RAG, memory, fallback, or fake production output.
Provider credential stores, default provider/model selection, or cross-provider retry.
stop_conditions: TASK-039 ordinary-task service cannot accept the matched envelope/classification handoff without widening its action or authorization boundary.
A competence-specific request cannot be executed without adding forbidden business/auth fields or widening generic ProviderRequestV1.
The canonical Safety classifier cannot preserve the service-side proposed task kind for exact post-classification matching.
Production composition would require fake/canned output, provider fallback, caller prompts, raw Task text in an instruction channel, or direct action authority.
Existing uncommitted work makes shared provider/main/package edits unsafe to reconcile.

constraints: TaskFollowUpProviderRequestV1 contains only the canonical definition, trigger, backend-allowed ordinary kinds, and one to four authorized PostgreSQL task/outcome/evidence records with matching ordered refs.
Task text is an explicit typed untrusted quotation and never an instruction, prompt, tool, command, authorization, evidence fact, or route selector.
The model result may speak only one allowed check, measurement, or follow_up proposal or produce strict model-declared silence; action and every mutation field are schema-invalid.
A non-silent result creates only a pending task_request MessageEnvelope; the existing project classifier must persist the exact same safe_task_kind before TASK-039 may create a Task.

The strict provider-neutral seam has no selected provider/model/base URL; production remains unbound and fail-closed, test fakes/spies are explicit, I/O is outside transactions, and every owning writer repeats current guards.

The task_follow_up runtime stage writes only the additive ft012_runtime_dispositions authority after model I/O under a short run-key advisory lock; the same lock and exact handed-off identity are required by the downstream classified Task writer, and no transaction/lock spans Task model or Safety-classifier I/O.
W1 record_follow_up_outcome keeps its closed evidence resolver and rejects task:/outcome: refs; W2 Task/Outcome source-record lookup is competence-specific and cannot be reused by the Outcome writer.

Deterministic acceptance requires exact task_follow_up and Safety fake/spy calls plus exactly one ordinary Task; fallback, production fake, silence, blocked, failed, mismatch, or direct action effect is not acceptance.
invariants: Model output, its proposed kind, MessageEnvelope, and classification are candidate/routing data; only the current TASK-039 ordinary-task service writes mutable Task authority.
The task_follow_up agent can never create action, approve or reject, complete a Task, record an Outcome, confirm Plant state, or produce a device effect.
UI Feed, Bus history, Timeline replay, raw chat, ActorContext/session/grant payloads, caller refs, prompts, provider history, hidden reasoning, and credentials never enter provider input.
Archived or unauthorized Plant state creates no model-backed Task effect and restore never replays the denied run.

One run/fingerprint has exactly one immutable runtime-stage disposition; publication_denied and the same run's classified consumed/denied state cannot coexist, and envelope_handed_off never mints or replays a second message.
Test fakes/spies are explicit seams only; no fake, canned, hardcoded, fallback, or failure-silence production path satisfies acceptance.
verification_targets: Strict request/result tests prove exact record union/order, allowed kinds, unknown-field rejection, typed quotation isolation, source-ref subsets, pending-envelope mapping, and orchestration nullability.
Outbound spies prove only authorized PostgreSQL Task/Outcome/evidence data crosses egress and every forbidden auth/UI/Bus/Timeline/prompt/provider field is absent.

Integration tests prove exact proposed-kind/classification-kind matching, one ordinary Task on success, identical retry, mismatch/physical/block conflict no effect, and no action/approval/completion/Outcome/Plant/device authority.
Authorization tests prove current pre/post-I/O, classifier, task-write, session/grant revoke, wrong-Farm, and archive races fail closed with no restore replay.

PostgreSQL tests prove exact runtime-disposition schema/migration head, command fingerprint, identical denied retry, changed-input conflict, concurrent same-run first-write, post-model archive/revoke durability, audit/commit rollback, runtime/classified exclusion, one post-guard message, and new-identity eligibility.
Regression tests prove task:/outcome: are accepted only by the competence source resolver and remain rejected by W1 record_follow_up_outcome evidence validation.

Provider-neutral tests prove explicit test fake/spy construction, exact call counts and allowlists, timeout/provider-error/invalid-output handling, unbound-production failure, no default/fallback/fake production output, redacted logs/audit/evidence, and compatibility with the existing Agent Runtime outcome matrix.
